Heritage sites by state

Heritage sites in Rajasthan: hill forts, Jaipur and ancient temples

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Updated 15 October 2026

Rajasthan has four UNESCO World Heritage listings: the Hill Forts of Rajasthan (Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Gagron, Amber and Jaisalmer), the Jantar Mantar in Jaipur, Jaipur City, and Keoladeo National Park, a natural site. Beyond them lie the Harappan town of Kalibangan, Ashokan Bairat, the temples of Osian, Dilwara and Ranakpur, and the old cities of Udaipur, Jodhpur and Bundi.

Our Forts of Rajasthan tour visits the UNESCO hill forts with an archaeologist, and we build custom Rajasthan itineraries for schools and private groups.

Rajasthan's heritage at a glance

Rajasthan is best known for the forts and palaces of the Rajput states, but its history is much deeper. Stone Age tools come from the Aravallis and the Thar, Harappan and earlier settlements line the dry bed of the Ghaggar at Kalibangan, copper-using cultures flourished at Ahar and Ganeshwar, and Ashoka left edicts at Bairat. From about the 8th century, temple building in the Maru-Gurjara style produced Osian, Kiradu and later the marble Jain temples of Mount Abu and Ranakpur.

The forts and walled cities came after, from the 13th to the 18th centuries, and Jaipur, founded in 1727, was one of India's first planned cities of the early modern period. Our explainer on forts of India sets them in context.

Museums in Rajasthan

  • Albert Hall Museum, Jaipur. Rajasthan's oldest museum, with sculpture, textiles and arms.
  • Mehrangarh Museum, Jodhpur. Palanquins, arms, paintings and textiles in the fort palace.
  • Ahar Museum, Udaipur. Finds from the Ahar excavations and early sculpture.
  • Kalibangan Site Museum. Harappan finds from the excavations.

UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Rajasthan

The Hill Forts of Rajasthan were inscribed together in 2013. Chittorgarh is a vast fort on a mesa, with the 15th century Vijay Stambha and Kirti Stambha. Kumbhalgarh's walls run for many kilometres along Aravalli ridges. Ranthambore sits inside a tiger reserve, Gagron is a water fort at the meeting of two rivers, Amber overlooks Jaipur and Jaisalmer is a living fort still home to residents.

Jaipur has two listings: the Jantar Mantar (2010), Sawai Jai Singh II's set of masonry astronomical instruments, and the walled city of Jaipur (2019) with its grid plan and bazaars. Keoladeo National Park at Bharatpur (1985) is a natural site, a wetland famous for migratory birds. Our tour Forts of Rajasthan visits several of the hill forts with an archaeologist, and Jaipur Jantar Mantar: instruments and observation explains how the instruments work.

Archaeological sites: Kalibangan, Bairat and Ahar

Kalibangan in Hanumangarh district has a pre-Harappan settlement with a ploughed field, one of the earliest found in South Asia, and a Harappan town with a citadel and fire altars. Bairat (Viratnagar) near Jaipur has Ashokan inscriptions and the remains of a circular Buddhist shrine, one of the earliest known structural temples. Ahar near Udaipur gives its name to the Ahar-Banas copper-using culture of the 3rd and 2nd millennia BCE, and Ganeshwar in Sikar district has yielded large numbers of copper objects.

These sites need explanation on the ground because what remains is mostly low walls and mounds. Our Harappan Gujarat tour and the indus valley civilization explainer help put Kalibangan in context.

Ancient temples in Rajasthan

Osian, north of Jodhpur, has a cluster of temples from the 8th to 12th centuries, including the Sachiya Mata temple and the Mahavira Jain temple. Kiradu near Barmer has finely carved ruined temples. Baroli, near Rawatbhata, is an early medieval group with superb sculpture. The Dilwara temples at Mount Abu, built in white marble between the 11th and 13th centuries, are famous for their ceiling carving, and Ranakpur's 15th century Jain temple has a forest of carved pillars.

Pushkar's Brahma temple, Eklingji near Udaipur and the Jagat Ambika Mata temple are also worth a visit. Our lecture Nagara temple architecture is the best preparation for Rajasthan's temples.

Cities to walk: Jaipur, Udaipur, Jodhpur and Jaisalmer

Each of Rajasthan's old capitals rewards a walk. Jaipur's grid of bazaars and havelis is best seen early in the morning. Udaipur's City Palace and lakes, Jodhpur's Mehrangarh and the blue houses below, and Jaisalmer's living fort each show a different relationship between ruler, city and water. Bundi's stepwells and painted palace and Shekhawati's frescoed havelis are worth adding for longer trips.

Questions people ask

How many UNESCO World Heritage Sites are in Rajasthan?

Four listings: the Hill Forts of Rajasthan (2013), which include six forts, the Jantar Mantar in Jaipur (2010), Jaipur City (2019) and Keoladeo National Park (1985), which is a natural site. The cultural listings cover eight places in total.

Which forts are in the Hill Forts of Rajasthan listing?

Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Gagron, Amber and Jaisalmer. They were inscribed together in 2013 because they show how Rajput states used hills, rivers and forests for defence over several centuries.

What are the main archaeological sites in Rajasthan?

Kalibangan for its pre-Harappan and Harappan levels, Bairat for Ashokan inscriptions and an early Buddhist shrine, Ahar for the Ahar-Banas copper culture, and Ganeshwar for its copper objects.

Which are the most important ancient temples in Rajasthan?

The Osian temples, the Dilwara temples at Mount Abu, the Ranakpur Jain temple, Baroli, Kiradu, Eklingji and the Jagat Ambika Mata temple. Together they show the development of the Maru-Gurjara style of western India.
